title: Stuart Skinner signs 2-year contract with Jets: What could it mean for Connor Hellebuyck?
content:
Stuart Skinner is joining his third team in the last few months.

After being traded from his hometown Edmonton Oilers to the Pittsburgh Penguins in December, Skinner has signed a two-year, $3.75 million AAV deal with the Winnipeg Jets, the team announced Wednesday.

The Penguins had interest in retaining the 27-year-old goaltender, but given their wealth of young goaltending, they didn’t feel comfortable offering Skinner a long-term contract.

While Skinner’s numbers in Pittsburgh were modest — he had a 12-9-5 record with a 2.99 goals-against average and an .885 save percentage — he instantly became a beloved teammate. Given that locker-room impact, the Penguins would have enjoyed having him around their young goaltenders for another year.

They couldn’t commit to anything beyond a year, though, and given the league’s goaltending issues, it became clear Skinner would receive more money and term elsewhere.

Skinner made quite a name for himself before he arrived in Pittsburgh. The Edmonton native twice led the Oilers to the doorstep of a championship, only to fall to the Florida Panthers on both occasions. He played extremely well during the 2024 postseason but fell 2-1 in Game 7 in Florida. His play slipped during the 2025 playoffs.

A slow start to the 2025-26 season led the Oilers to trade Skinner to Pittsburgh in a deal that included another goalie, Tristan Jarry.

Skinner played well early for the Penguins, but his performance dipped following February’s Olympic break. He went 0-3 for the Penguins in the postseason.

Artūrs Šilovs and Sergei Murashov are expected to be the Penguins’ goaltenders to start the 2026-27 season, and another talented netminder — Joel Blomqvist — could also contend for playing time.

As much as the Penguins liked Skinner personally and found him reliable enough, they weren’t going to commit to him.

The Jets had no such issue. — Josh Yohe

Skinner wasn’t the No. 1 solution the Oilers needed during their Cup runs, but he has a career .902 save percentage and could be a capable 1B goaltender.

The big question is who’s meant to be Winnipeg’s No. 1. The most likely answer to that question is “whoever Winnipeg gets in return for Connor Hellebuyck.” Buffalo’s Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen appears to be the most likely candidate — if the Jets and Sabres are able to agree to a trade.

The 6-foot-6, left-catching goaltender was a teammate of Eric Comrie’s for two seasons in Buffalo, emerging as the Sabres’ 1A starter from a group of goalies that included Comrie and Devon Levi. But he struggled in the playoffs, briefly losing his crease to Alex Lyon, increasing the impetus to sign Skinner.

If Hellebuyck were likely to stay, the Jets’ simplest move would have been to sign his longtime backup, Comrie. If Hellebuyck were somehow convinced to stay, then Skinner’s $3.75 million cap hit would be manageable in a backup role. — Murat Ates
